stops.name: Buenos Aires, the sculptor is born
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the twenty-eighth of April a son is born in Buenos Aires to the Catalan painter Miguel Viladrich and to Ana Morera, a teacher of painting. They give him the Catalan spelling of the old name, Wifredo, not the Castilian Wilfredo; thirty-five years later he will model the hairy count who carried it first. The father paints Aragonese peasants with the finish of a Flemish primitive and is known on both sides of the ocean. The boy holds an Argentine birth certificate and will spend almost none of his childhood in the country that issued it.
stops.quote: Wifredo Viladrich nació en Buenos Aires el 28 de abril de 1923, hijo del pintor catalán Miguel Viladrich y la profesora Ana Morera.
suggested_refs: Wikidata Q110450265, Wifredo Viladrich, sourced to artedelaargentina.com
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica
Wikidata Q110450265 (b. 28 April 1923, Buenos Aires)

stops.name: Fraga, the Castillo de Urganda
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the family site; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Two years old, he is carried to Spain. The family settles at Fraga, on the Cinca in lower Aragón, in the house the painter has made his own and calls the Castillo de Urganda. His father's subjects are the people of that country, reapers and water carriers and girls with pitchers on the hip, and the boy learns the trade backward, from the sitters first. Thirty-seven years later, working in Buenos Aires, he will cast a small bronze and call her Fragatina, moza de cántaro, the girl of Fraga with the water jar.
stops.quote: La familia se trasladó a España en 1925, estableciéndose en el Castillo de Urganda, Fraga, Aragón.
suggested_refs: The house of Miguel Viladrich at Fraga, called the Castillo de Urganda
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica

stops.name: Morocco, two years across the strait
stops.date_confidence: years attested (1932-1934); no city named, no month or day
stops.campa: Between 1932 and 1934 the household lives in Morocco, across the strait from the Spain they have made home. He is nine when they go and eleven when they come back. Nothing he later carves is Moroccan; no city is named in the family's account of those years and no reason given for the move or the return. It is the first of the three uprootings of his childhood. The second empties the country they have just come back to, and the third puts him on a ship for Argentina at fifteen.
suggested_refs: Any Spanish-Moroccan residence record for the painter Miguel Viladrich, 1932-1934
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica

segments.name: War, and the Pyrenees on Foot

stops.name: Madrid, the family after Morocco
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the family account gives the sequence after 1934, no year
stops.campa: Back from Africa the family does not return to Fraga but to the capital. Madrid in these years is a Republic three years old and already fighting for its life, and the painter's son is eleven, then twelve, then thirteen. He is set to drawing, as painters' sons are. Before the war reaches them the household moves once more, to Barcelona, and the two cities together give him what an Aragonese village could not: academies, plaster casts, museums, and other people's hands to watch working.
suggested_refs: Madrid residence records for Miguel Viladrich, mid-1930s
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica (Madrid and Barcelona named, undated)

stops.name: Barcelona, the formation completed in a war
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the site says his formation was completed in Barcelona and that he lived the war between thirteen and fifteen; the day here is the rising in the city
stops.campa: In Barcelona he completes his artistic formation. He is thirteen in the July when the generals rise and the city answers them in the street; he will be fifteen when it starts to starve. The war is not a rumor carried to him. He lives inside it for its whole length, in the city that holds out longest, and it is in these three years that his hands finish learning what they know. The first full statue he ever completes, seven years later and an ocean away, will be a naked man in chains, and he will name it Pueblo Español.
stops.quote: Durante la Guerra Civil española, cuando tenía entre 13 y 15 años, Wifredo experimentó directamente los conflictos.
suggested_refs: Barcelona art school enrolment records, 1935-1938
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica

stops.name: Barcelona, out hours before the troops
stops.date_confidence: year attested (1939, hours before the Francoist occupation); the day here is the fall of Barcelona, not a dated family record
stops.campa: With the Francoist columns at the edge of the city the family walks out of Barcelona. They take the road north with the rest of it: hundreds of thousands of people on the highways to the frontier that winter, carts, mattresses, children, a country emptying itself into France. The painter of Fraga leaves behind the house he made and the country he spent his life painting. His son is fifteen. Argentina, which gave the boy a birth certificate and nothing else, is now the only open door the family has, and it is an ocean away.
stops.quote: En 1939, horas antes de que las tropas franquistas la ocuparan, salió con su familia de Barcelona. Cruzaron a pie los Pirineos, rumbo al exilio en la Argentina.
suggested_refs: Spanish Republican exile registers for the Viladrich family, 1939
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica

stops.name: The Pyrenees, crossed on foot
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the pass, the day, and the route to the ship are unrecorded
stops.campa: They cross the Pyrenees on foot. The passes in that month are snow to the knee and the road through them is a single file of the defeated; on the French side lie the beach camps of the Roussillon, sand, wire, and no roof. Which pass the Viladrich family takes, how long they are held, how they find a ship, none of it is written down in anything the family has published. What is written is one sentence: they crossed on foot, bound for exile in Argentina. He is fifteen, and the crossing is the last thing the record places him at in Europe for nineteen years.
suggested_refs: French internment camp registers at Argelès-sur-Mer and Saint-Cyprien, spring 1939
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica

stops.name: San Fernando del Valle de Catamarca, he begins to sculpt
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month defaulted to the first plausible after the crossing
stops.campa: The family lands in Argentina and goes not to Buenos Aires but to Catamarca, in the dry northwest under the Andes: a province of adobe, irrigation ditches, poplars, and faces the colonial centuries never finished remaking. Here, at sixteen, Wifredo begins to sculpt. He has been in the country a few months. His first subjects are not the war he has walked out of and not Spain; they are the people of the valley he has landed in, and for ten years almost everything he makes will be a face from the northwest.
suggested_refs: Catamarca provincial records of the Viladrich family, 1939-1944
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica

stops.name: Catamarca, El Guaica, muchacho catamarqueño
stops.date_confidence: contested: the research pool dates the bust 1940 at age seventeen; the artist's own records date only the 1942 prize and a 1949 museum version
stops.campa: At seventeen he models the head of a Catamarcan boy and calls it El Guaica. It is a bust of nobody famous, a local face done by a foreigner who has been in the province a year, and it is the work that makes him a sculptor. In 1942 it takes an encouragement prize at the thirty-second national salon in Buenos Aires; in 1949 an acquisition prize on the coast, after which it stays in the municipal museum of Mar del Plata. A boy who crossed the Pyrenees in the snow puts a boy from Catamarca into bronze and is let into Argentine art by him.
suggested_refs: El Guaica, muchacho catamarqueño, Museo Municipal, Mar del Plata
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos
wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the encouragement prize at the XXXII Salón
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given in the prize list
stops.campa: Nineteen years old, three years off the boat, he sends El Guaica to the thirty-second annual salon of fine arts in Buenos Aires and takes the encouragement prize for sculpture. The salon is the only ladder in Argentine art and he has put his foot on its first rung with the head of a boy from Catamarca. He was born in this city and has not lived in it since he was two. Within two years he will move back for good and begin the career the prize lists record, year by year, purchase by purchase, for the next twenty-four.
stops.quote: PREMIO ESTÍMULO, XXXII SALÓN ANUAL DE BELLAS ARTES
stops.quote_source: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos, 1942, for EL GUAICA - MUCHACHO CATAMARQUEÑO
suggested_refs: Catalogue of the XXXII Salón Anual de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires, 1942
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos
wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica

stops.name: Buenos Aires, he settles in the capital
stops.date_confidence: year attested (from 1944 he resided in Buenos Aires); month and day defaulted
stops.campa: From 1944 he lives in Buenos Aires and stays. He is twenty-one. The city he returns to is filling with people out of the provinces, and he arrives as one more of them, a Spaniard by upbringing with a Catamarcan accent in his work. He teaches as well as sculpts, as his mother taught before him. From here the map of his life narrows to a short circuit: the studio, the salons, the plazas of small municipalities, and eventually the jury rooms where the monuments of the republic are decided.
stops.quote: Desde 1944 residió en Buenos Aires, donde continuó su carrera artística y docente.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires studio and teaching records for Viladrich, 1944 onward
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Hijo de la tierra, Jujuy
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: He sends a bust called Hijo de la tierra, Jujuy to the municipal salon and takes second prize, with the acquisition; the head goes into the Sívori collection, the first of his works to enter a public museum in the capital. Son of the earth: another northwestern face, from the province above Catamarca, made by a man who has been Argentine on paper since birth and Argentine in fact for five years. The country that is taking him in he keeps portraying from its poorest and highest edge.
suggested_refs: Museo de Artes Plásticas Eduardo Sívori, holdings of Hijo de la tierra, Jujuy
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos
wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Pueblo Español and the jury
stops.date_confidence: 1946 attested for the affair; the statue is dated only by his age, twenty-two
stops.campa: At twenty-two he finishes his first full statue: a naked man in chains, and its name is Pueblo Español. In 1946 it makes a noise. The jury of the municipal salon will exhibit it and give it a prize on one condition, that the name come off; Franco's Spain is a government Buenos Aires does business with, the Spanish people is a man in chains, and the two things cannot stand in the same room. He refuses. The statue is neither shown nor awarded, and his prize list, unbroken on either side, records nothing at all for that year.
stops.quote: A los veintidós años concluyó su primera estatua, Pueblo Español, imagen de un hombre desnudo y encadenado, que adquirió en 1946 gran repercusión: Wifredo se negó a cambiarle el nombre, como le exigiera el jurado como condición para ser expuesta y premiada en el Salón Municipal.
suggested_refs: Salón Municipal de Buenos Aires jury minutes, 1946

sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Síntesis biográfica

stops.name: Mar del Plata, El Guaica bought by the coast
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: The Catamarcan boy's head travels to the sea. At the eighth art salon of Mar del Plata it takes the acquisition prize and stays, entering the municipal museum of a city built for summer people, a thousand miles east of the valley it was modeled in. Mar del Plata will be the city that gives him his largest commissions: two of the three competitions of his last years are held for its seafront. The relationship begins here, with a nine-year-old bust of a boy from the Andes bought by a bathing resort.
suggested_refs: Catalogue of the VIII Salón de Arte de Mar del Plata, 1949
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos
wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Bahía Blanca, Hombre de Belén
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: The same year, at the fourth salon of Bahía Blanca, the port at the bottom of the pampa, he takes second prize with a figure called Hombre de Belén, the man from Belén: another Catamarcan town, another face out of the northwest, shown fifteen hundred kilometers south of where it lives. Ten years after the Pyrenees his name is known to the juries of three provinces, and every work they know it by is a poor man of the northwest, modeled by a Spaniard who landed there at sixteen.
suggested_refs: Catalogue of the IV Salón de Bahía Blanca, 1949
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos

stops.name: Mar del Plata, Chacho el boyero
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: At the ninth Mar del Plata salon he takes an encouragement prize with Chacho, el boyero, the ox driver: a working man with his animals, the third of his provincial types in two years. He is twenty-seven. The shape of his working life is fixed now and will hold for two decades, heads and figures of country people sent out to the salons, a prize or a purchase most years, museums and municipalities buying one at a time. The monuments, the plazas, the sealed competition envelopes are all still twenty years off.
suggested_refs: Catalogue of the IX Salón de Arte de Mar del Plata, 1950
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos

segments.name: The Count, the Gaucho, and the Mothers

stops.name: Barcelona, two works for the Argentine consulate
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: Nineteen years after he walked out of the city, two of his works are installed in the Argentine consulate at Barcelona: a relief of José de San Martín, who freed one country and crossed the Andes to free two more, and a statuette of Wifredo el Velloso, the hairy count, first sovereign of Catalonia and the man whose name he carries. Argentina's liberator and Catalonia's founder stand by the same hand in the building where Catalans go for the papers that will take them to Buenos Aires. Nothing in the record says he travels with them.
stops.quote: Wifredo el Velloso (estatuilla), 1958, Consulado Argentino, Barcelona
stops.quote_source: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos
suggested_refs: Argentine consulate, Barcelona: the San Martín relief and the Wifredo el Velloso statuette
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Viejo Criollo at the XLIX Salón
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: At the forty-ninth national salon he takes an honorable mention in historical art with a figure called Viejo Criollo, listed with a second title in brackets: Martín Fierro. The gaucho of José Hernández's poem, the deserter, the knife fighter, the voice of everything the republic was built by pushing aside, is by now the national self-portrait, and Viladrich, born in Buenos Aires, raised in Aragón, made a sculptor in Catamarca, models him as an old criollo. He will come back to Fierro once more, twenty years after his own death.
suggested_refs: Catalogue of the XLIX Salón Nacional de Artes Plásticas, 1960
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos

stops.name: New York, Fragatina at the Hispanic Society
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: A small bronze of his enters the Hispanic Society of America on Audubon Terrace in upper Manhattan, the museum built to hold Spain in New York. Its title is Fragatina, moza de cántaro, a girl of Fraga with a water jar. He is thirty-nine and has not seen the town since he was fifteen. Of the three hundred and eighty-three works he will leave, this one travels farthest and is the only one that looks back at Fraga: a village on the Cinca modeled from memory in Buenos Aires and shelved in an American's collection of Spain.
stops.quote: Fragatina, moza de cántaro (estatuilla), 1962, Museo Hispanic Society, New York
stops.quote_source: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos
suggested_refs: Hispanic Society of America accession records for Fragatina, moza de cántaro
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Lanús, the monument to Sarmiento
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given; the pin is the town centre, not the plaza
stops.campa: In the industrial suburb of Lanús, south of the capital, his monument to Domingo Faustino Sarmiento is raised: the schoolmaster president who wanted the country filled with immigrants and their children put into classrooms, commemorated in a town made of exactly that. Viladrich is forty-one and this is public sculpture now, standing in a street rather than lit in a room. The change holds. From here he works to scale, for municipalities, and the salon figures continue beside the monuments in a smaller key.
suggested_refs: Municipality of Lanús records for the Sarmiento monument, 1964
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Pacha Mama in stone
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: He cuts a head in stone and calls it Pacha Mama, the earth mother of the Andes; it takes the Justina and Manuel Quinquela prize for sculpture at the fifty-fifth national salon, and the national culture directorate buys it the same year. The year is the best of his life for prizes: a third comes from the municipal salon for a girl with a drum. Twenty-seven years after Catamarca he is still working the northwest, no longer as a newcomer's subject but as a language, and he is doing it now in stone he cuts rather than clay he builds.
suggested_refs: Dirección Nacional de Cultura acquisition record for Pacha Mama, 1966
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos
wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Vicente López, the fifth Monument to the Mother
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: In the riverside suburb north of the capital he raises another Monument to the Mother, the fifth of them. The first went to a village in Santa Fe in 1963, one to Lima in Buenos Aires province in 1965, one to María Teresa in 1968, and in this year two, here and at Sancti Spíritu. Five towns order the same subject from the same man in seven years. It is the working sculptor's bread: a figure a municipality can afford, a Sunday for the unveiling, a plaque, a plaza, and a woman in bronze standing in it as long as the town lasts.
suggested_refs: The five Monumentos a la Madre: Christophersen 1963, Lima 1965, María Teresa 1968, Vicente López 1970, Sancti Spíritu 1970
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Buenos Aires, first prize for the Pueyrredón monument
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: He wins the competition for a monument to Juan Martín de Pueyrredón: first prize and the award of the work. The Supreme Director who provisioned San Martín's army for the crossing of the Andes, and then quarreled with him past repair, has been dead a hundred and twenty years and is owed a plaza in the capital. Viladrich is forty-seven. In the three years that follow he will win four national competitions and change register completely, from boys of Catamarca and mothers of small towns to the founders of the country in heroic bronze.
stops.quote: 1º PREMIO y ADJUDICACIÓN - Monumento General Pueyrredón
suggested_refs: Competition records for the Pueyrredón monument, Buenos Aires, 1970
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos

stops.name: Buenos Aires, second prize for the Güemes monument
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: The same year he takes second prize in the competition for a monument to Martín Miguel de Güemes, the gaucho general who held the northern frontier against the royalist armies with irregular cavalry and his own fortune, and who lies buried in Salta, in the country where Viladrich learned to sculpt. The commission goes to another hand. He is now a man the juries know by name, entering everything, placed in everything, and within a year he will take both first and second prize in a single competition on the coast.
suggested_refs: Competition records for the Güemes monument, 1970, and the name of the winning sculptor
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos

stops.name: Plaza República de Chile, the Pueyrredón monument stands
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given; the pin is approximate to the plaza, unverified against a gazetteer
stops.campa: The monument goes up in Plaza República de Chile in the capital, in the same barrio as the cemetery where his best-known work will stand within two years. It is his first monument in Buenos Aires. He is forty-eight, he has lived in the city since he was twenty-one, and this is the first thing of his a person can find in it without going indoors. The prize list calls the award 1º Premio y Adjudicación, first prize and the grant of the work, a phrase that will repeat three times in four years and then never again.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires city monument register, Plaza República de Chile
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Mar del Plata, both prizes for the Admiral Brown competition
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: The competition for a monument to Admiral Guillermo Brown, the Irishman who built the Argentine navy out of merchant hulls and privateers, is decided on the coast, and Viladrich's name appears twice on the result: first prize with the award of the work, and second prize as well. He has entered the same competition more than once and beaten himself into second place. The monument is his. Six years and one death will pass before it stands in the place the jury chose for it.
stops.quote: 1º PREMIO y ADJUDICACIÓN - Monumento Almirante Brown, Mar del Plata
suggested_refs: Mar del Plata municipal competition records for the Almirante Brown monument, 1971
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos

stops.name: Mar del Plata, first prize for Alas de la Patria
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: A year later the same city holds a competition for a monument called Alas de la Patria, the Wings of the Fatherland, for the fliers of the republic, and he wins it outright. It is the fourth competition in three years and the third first prize. He is forty-nine and has four years to live, and neither he nor the juries know it. The work he has in hand at this exact moment for a private family in Recoleta, a bride in a wedding dress with her hand resting on a dog, is the one the country will actually remember him by.
suggested_refs: Mar del Plata competition records for Alas de la Patria, 1972
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Premios obtenidos

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the wings raised
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: The wings go up on the coast in 1973, the only one of his three great late commissions he lives to see standing. Mar del Plata in that decade is the republic's summer capital, a seafront of casinos and rambla and a million holidaymakers a season, and he has put a monument into it in the year the old president comes home from his own exile. He is fifty, and he has been working at this trade for thirty-four years, since a valley in Catamarca. The catalogue of his public works ends here in his lifetime; every entry dated after 1973 goes up without him.
suggested_refs: Mar del Plata seafront monument register, A las Alas de la Patria, 1973
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Hotel Piz Buin, Tyrol, the avalanche
stops.date_confidence: date attested; the hotel's position is given only as some sixty-four kilometres west of Innsbruck, and the pin here is the Silvretta gateway village of Galtür
stops.campa: On the twenty-sixth of February an avalanche comes down on a hotel in the Tyrolean Alps, in a valley west of Innsbruck under the Silvretta. Liliana Crociati de Szaszak of Buenos Aires, twenty-six years old, newly married to Janos Szaszak, is inside it. She dies; her husband lives. She was born in 1944, the year Viladrich moved to Buenos Aires and put his first bust into a public museum there. They have never met and never will, and her parents are about to make her the subject of his most looked-at work.
suggested_refs: Austrian avalanche records for the Paznaun and Silvretta valleys, February 1970
sources: en.wikipedia.org, Tomb of Liliana Crociati de Szaszak
es.wikipedia.org, Tumba de Liliana Crociati de Szaszak

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Crociati family comes to the sculptor
stops.date_confidence: contested: the press dates the commission to the weeks after the February 1970 death, the artist's own catalogue dates the bronze 1972; 1971 is placed here for order only
stops.campa: Her mother will design the tomb herself and her father will write what is written on it. What they need is the daughter, and they come for her to Viladrich, who at this moment is winning the monument competitions of the republic. Life size, in the wedding dress, wearing the ring she was married in. The press tells it as a father's commission given in the weeks after the avalanche; the sculptor's own catalogue dates the bronze two years later. The two accounts have never been reconciled, and the tomb itself carries no date at all.
suggested_refs: Barbara Cansino, Cemetery For the Elite of Argentina, The New York Times, 10 January 1999
sources: en.wikipedia.org, Tomb of Liliana Crociati de Szaszak
wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Recoleta, the chapel of wood and glass
stops.date_confidence: undated in every reachable source; placed with the statue for order
stops.campa: In a cemetery of granite and shut marble, in avenues where the vaults face each other like houses on a street and let in no light at all, Liliana's mother builds a small neo-Gothic chapel of wood and glass, with windows wide enough to see through. The dead of Recoleta are kept in the dark by custom; this one is kept where the sun can reach her. The mother draws it, the sculptor fills it, the father sets a dais beside the figure. It is the one house in the necropolis built to be looked into rather than at.
suggested_refs: The neo-Gothic Crociati crypt, Cementerio de la Recoleta
sources: en.wikipedia.org, Tomb of Liliana Crociati de Szaszak
es.wikipedia.org, Tumba de Liliana Crociati de Szaszak

stops.name: Recoleta, the bronze bride
stops.date_confidence: 1972 per the artist's own catalogue; en.wikipedia gives no year and the press implies 1970
stops.campa: He casts her life size in bronze and lets the metal go green. She stands in her wedding dress with the ring on her finger, twenty-six years old for good, in a glass chapel in the middle of the most photographed cemetery in South America. His catalogue of public works gives her one line, between the admiral and the wings. Of the three hundred and eighty-three works he makes, this is the one that becomes a place: people come to Recoleta to see her who could not name another thing he made, and most of them never learn his name at all.
stops.quote: Liliana Crociati (1972) – Cementerio Recoleta, Ciudad de Buenos Aires
stops.quote_source: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos
suggested_refs: The bronze figure of Liliana Crociati de Szaszak in her wedding dress, Cementerio de la Recoleta
sources: wifredoviladrich.com, Listado de obras en lugares públicos

stops.name: Recoleta, A Mia Figlia on the dais
stops.date_confidence: undated; placed with the statue
stops.campa: Beside the bronze her father sets a dais with a poem on it, in Italian, in his own words, addressed to her: A Mia Figlia, To My Daughter. It asks the same question in different words, over and over, and no line in it answers. A father who writes, a mother who draws, and a sculptor who is at that moment casting admirals: three trades brought to bear on one twenty-six-year-old, in a language that is not the country's, in a cemetery where every other family speaks in marble and in Latin.

stops.name: Recoleta, Sabú added in bronze
stops.date_confidence: undated: no source gives the year of the dog's death or of the second casting, only that it follows the first
stops.campa: Her dog outlives her. When Sabú dies they bring the sculptor back and he makes the animal too, and sets him under her right hand, so that the bride stands with her fingers resting on the head of her dog. No source records the year the dog dies or the year the second bronze arrives. It is the only commission he takes twice for the same family, and the last work of his own to be catalogued in his lifetime: a girl killed by a mountain, a dog dead of old age, and one hand joining them in a place where nothing else touches anything.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, death at fifty-three
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the thirteenth of May he dies in Buenos Aires, fifty-three years old, in the city he was born in and hardly lived in until he was twenty-one. He leaves three hundred and eighty-three works: reliefs, statuettes, portraits, busts, statues, monuments. Commissions of his are still unraised at his death, one of them the admiral he won twice, and they will go up without him. The competitions of 1970, 1971, and 1972 turn out to have been the whole of his monumental career, four years wide, and he did not know he was working against a clock.
stops.quote: una producción escultórica de trescientas ochenta y tres obras entre relieves, estatuillas, retratos, bustos, estatuas y monumentos

stops.name: Rambla Casino, Mar del Plata, the admiral in the dry plaza
stops.date_confidence: contested: es.wikipedia dates the installation 1977, the artist's own catalogue dates the monument 1972; both may be true of a work finished in one year and raised in another
stops.campa: A year after his death his Admiral Brown is set up in the dry plaza of the Rambla Casino complex at Mar del Plata, filling the space Alejandro Bustillo had left empty in his design, where the architect imagined a single monolithic obelisk standing. His catalogue dates the monument to 1972; the record of the plaza dates the installation to 1977. Nobody has explained the gap. The bronze occupies an architect's blank and the sculptor is not there for either version of the date.

stops.name: Barcelona, the Andean flute player at the city hall
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: Three years dead, he arrives at the city hall of Barcelona: a figure called Humahuaqueño, Indio de la quena, a man of the Humahuaca gorge with a cane flute. Forty years after he walked out of this city at fifteen, hours ahead of the troops, a bronze Andean flute player of his stands in its municipality. He left Catalonia carrying nothing. What comes back in his name is a man off the far northern frontier of the country that took him in, and he is not there to hand it over.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the wings raised a second time
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: The wings go up again, now in the capital, eight years after the Mar del Plata original and five years after the sculptor's death. Argentina in 1981 is a year away from a war over islands in the south, and a monument to the fliers of the fatherland is a thing a government can use. The hand that modeled it has been in the ground since 1976. From here his works are raised on other people's occasions, in other people's decades, and there is nobody left to say what any of them were made for.

stops.name: Río Cuarto, the heroes of Malvinas
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given
stops.campa: In the garrison city of Río Cuarto in Córdoba a monument to the heroes of Malvinas is raised and it is his: eight years after his death, two years after the war, by a man who died before the islands were taken and who crossed the Pyrenees at fifteen out of somebody else's war. The catalogue lists it flat with the rest, by year and place. What stood finished in the studio when he died, what was cast afterward from his models, and by whose hands, the record does not say.

stops.name: General Madariaga, Martín Fierro in gaucho country
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not given; the pin is the town centre
stops.campa: Twenty years after his death a monument of his to Martín Fierro is raised at General Madariaga, in horse country on the Atlantic side of Buenos Aires province, thirty-six years after the old criollo he showed at the national salon in 1960. The deserter of José Hernández's poem, in bronze, in a town of riders. Two further works follow at Pinamar, in 2001 and in 2018, the last of them forty-two years after the sculptor died. The models outlive the hands and keep arriving.

stops.name: Recoleta, the polished muzzle
stops.date_confidence: the custom itself is undated; 2019 is the date of the press feature that records it
stops.campa: Sabú's nose is bright. The rest of the two bronzes is green with fifty years of weather and that one place is rubbed back to raw metal by hands, because it is held in the city that touching the dog's snout brings luck. Nobody records who started it. The tomb has a name of its own now, la novia de la Recoleta, the bride of Recoleta, and the guidebooks send people to it; a New York paper wrote it up in 1999, a Canadian paper in 2007, the Buenos Aires press in 2019. What they photograph is a bride, a dog, and a shine.
stops.quote: El hocico del perro suele verse brillante ya que existe la creencia popular de que tocarlo trae buena suerte.

stops.name: Recoleta, the parents laid beside her
stops.date_confidence: undated: both parents are recorded as interred with their daughter, with no year given in any reachable source; placed at the 2019 feature that records the fact, for ordering only
stops.campa: In their own time the mother who drew the chapel and the father who wrote the poem are laid inside it beside their daughter. No source gives the years. The family that ordered one statue and then a second for the dog ends up entirely within the small glass house, three of them and an animal in bronze, in a necropolis where the great vaults hold ten generations of ministers and generals and are visited by nobody. Theirs is the one with people waiting outside it in the avenue, cameras up, on any ordinary morning.

stops.name: Recoleta, four spellings of one name
stops.date_confidence: state of the record as consulted in 2026
stops.campa: The most looked-at work in the cemetery is signed by a man nobody can spell. The English article on the tomb calls him Wíeredovol Viladrich, which is a word in no language; a Canadian newspaper called him Wilfredo; the Spanish article on the tomb writes Wílfredo, and the Spanish article on the Mar del Plata monument writes Wilfredo again. His family's own catalogue and the record built from it give Wifredo, the Catalan form, the count's name, the one he carved in Barcelona in 1958. Four spellings, one hand.
